summary: 1934 CCC-built Aermotor fire tower in Robinson Forest, Breathitt County, Kentucky; NHLR-registered 1996 and described as staffed. Current staffing not confirmed by a second source.

access.note: A public trail leads to the tower, but no source read says whether the tower itself may be climbed.

visit.trail_note: Boardinghouse Trail, 0.9 mile, gains 660 feet on its way to the fire tower

facts.agency: Department of Forestry, University of Kentucky

events.note: Built by the CCC, per the Register; the university history dates CCC fire-tower work to 1933-1937
Replaced two wooden towers and the Tip Rock observation site

evidence.supports: Robinson Forest is a University of Kentucky forest

evidence.quote: was built by the CCC in 1934

evidence.supports: replaced two wooden towers and the Tip Rock observation site
evidence.quote: replacing two wooden towers and the Tip Rock observation site

evidence.supports: Kentucky once had more than 100 state towers
evidence.quote: The woodlands of Kentucky were once covered by a network of more than 100 state towers

evidence.supports: one tower remains in active service
evidence.quote: now there is one that remains in active service

evidence.supports: staffed by the Department of Forestry at the University of Kentucky
evidence.quote: It is staffed by the Department of Forestry at the University of Kentucky

evidence.supports: nominated by Robert Muller of the UK Forestry Dept.
CCC built fire towers in the forest between 1933 and 1937
evidence.quote: Between 1933 and 1937, the Civilian Conservation Corps was involved in projects such as building bridges, fire towers, and firebreaks

evidence.supports: trail is 0.9 mile and gains 660 feet
evidence.quote: The 0.9 mile trail gains 660 feet in elevation

evidence.quote: to the fire tower at the top of the hill

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register gives 1934 and the university history gives a 1933-1937 CCC window; the 1934 date falls inside that window, so the sources agree.

notes_for_editor: Unresolved conflict on height and status. A University of Kentucky Forestry Facebook post surfaced in search (https://www.facebook.com/UKYFNR/posts/an-iconic-symbol-from-robinson-forest-the-999-fire-tower-was-constructed-by-the-/1285420921504903/) gives the height as 99 feet 9 inches and says the tower no longer serves in its original capacity as a fire lookout. The page returned a login stub, so it is not cited and the story does not rely on it. The NHLR says 100 feet and in active service. Check that post before publishing. The Wikipedia Robinson Forest article has a 'Robinson Forest Fire Tower' heading over a CCC paragraph only; it was not cited. The brief's record has no build event, so 1934 is added. No corrections to the brief.
